question.problem:
Consider the system of equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x-9y+4z=1 \\ 3x-2y-5z=7 \\ 3x-8y+2z=5.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}$, where $D$ is the determinant of the coefficient matrix and ${D}_{z}=$
question.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+(-9)y+4z=1 \\ 3x+(-2)y+(-5)z=7 \\ 3x+(-8)y+2z=5.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
D=|\begin{aligned}2 & -9 & 4 \\ 3 & -2 & -5 \\ 3 & -8 & 2\end{aligned}|.
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{z}$, we replace the third column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}2 & -9 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 7 \\ 3 & -8 & 5\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
